title: Kagome lattice candidate URhSn: Measured Bragg diffraction patterns and theory for hexagonal and trigonal Sohncke phases
authors: S. W. Lovesey, D. D. Khalyavin
abstract: Ternary intermetallics use a ZrNiAl-type chemical structure known as a kagome system. Complexity observed in the phase diagrams of these compounds is attributed to the geometric frustration. The 5f-electron compound URhSn exhibits two phase transitions at 16 K and 54 K. No super-lattice reflections in neutron powder diffraction patterns are detected in the intermediate range of temperatures (16 K - 54 K). Recent resonant x-ray diffraction patterns for uranium ions in the intermediate phase suggest a chiral structure and a trigonal Sohncke space group. It is firmly established that a simple hexagonal space group describes the parent structure at room temperature. A ferroic order parameter that includes hexadecapoles is shown to characterize the trigonal Sohncke phase. Resonant x-ray diffraction by this phase is fully investigated with our symmetry informed theory. It repairs symmetry in the original data analysis by using a grey group, and it lifts an unjustified spatial condition on uranium positions. The theory uses axial atomic multipoles that satisfy sum-rules established in the first instance for x-ray dichroic signals. A confrontation between observed and calculated diffraction patterns lends support to a trigonal Sohncke phase, and exposes grounds for additional experimental work on an enigmatic compound.
summary: This work analyzes the structural phases of the 5f-electron compound URhSn, which exhibits complex behavior due to geometric frustration. By combining neutron and resonant x-ray diffraction, the authors propose that an intermediate phase adopts a trigonal Sohncke structure. This finding is supported by advanced symmetry-informed theory applied to the diffraction data.
main_problem: The paper investigates the structural and electronic complexity of the 5f-electron compound URhSn, which belongs to the kagome system, and its phase transitions.
main_result: The resonant x-ray diffraction patterns suggest that the intermediate phase adopts a chiral structure belonging to the trigonal Sohncke space group, characterized by a ferroic order parameter including hexadecapoles.
method: The study combines neutron powder diffraction (to check for super-lattice reflections) with resonant x-ray diffraction, employing a symmetry-informed theoretical framework.
model_or_system: The physical system is the ternary intermetallic compound URhSn, which exhibits phase transitions at 16 K and 54 K. The parent structure is described by a simple hexagonal space group.
key_observables: Bragg diffraction patterns (neutron and resonant x-ray), super-lattice reflections, and x-ray dichroic signals.
important_parameters: Temperature (phase transitions at 16 K and 54 K), and the presence of 5f electrons.
main_assumptions: The theory uses axial atomic multipoles satisfying established sum-rules for x-ray dichroic signals, and the analysis corrects for potential symmetry issues in initial data processing.
figures_summary: The notes do not provide a summary of figures, only the methodology and conclusions drawn from comparing observed and calculated diffraction patterns.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the parent structure (hexagonal), observes phase transitions, uses neutron diffraction to rule out super-lattice reflections in an intermediate range, and then applies advanced resonant x-ray diffraction theory to support the trigonal Sohncke phase.
why_interesting: The investigation of complex magnetic/structural ordering (ferroic order parameter, hexadecapoles) in a strongly correlated 5f-electron material like URhSn is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phases in condensed matter systems.
